# 玉籙大齋第一日午朝儀-宋

**ID:** KR5b0202
**Custom ID:** ZB5b0202

**Editions:** SJB, ZHDZ

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

Second of the eight-part **Yùlù dàzhāi** programme (DZ 505 a–h = [KR5b0201](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b0201)–[KR5b0208](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b0208)). The fascicle contains the noon audience of the opening day; together with the morning ([KR5b0201](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b0201)) and evening ([KR5b0203](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b0203)) audiences it completes the three offices of day one of the three-day fast.

**Abstract**

The noon rite repeats the structural skeleton of the morning audience — *fālú*, *qǐngchēng fǎwèi*, three *niǎnxiāng* with the imperial-longevity / ancestral-shrines / cosmos dedications — but is differentiated by its position in the *sānyuán* 三元 (three-prime) cosmological scheme. The noon audience, falling at the *zhōngyuán* 中元 of the day, is keyed to the *Tàiyī jiùkǔ* 太一救苦 and the central-axis pole, while preserving the standard *Yùlù* dedication to the *Dōngjí Qīngxuán* 東極青玄 (Eastern-Polar Mysterious-Pure) deities who receive the deceased. The body of the text comprises the standard noon hymns (*Língbǎo zhēnwén* 靈寳真文 etc.), the *zhuǎnjīng* 轉經 recitation of the *Dùrén* / *Jiùkǔ* 救苦 scriptures, and the *huíxiàng* dedication of the cumulative merit.

Per Schipper & Verellen (*Taoist Canon* 2: 1004–1006, John Lagerwey, DZ 505), the strict three-times-three division of *Yùlù* worship is the diagnostic feature of the Sòng-Yuán *Yùlù* programme and distinguishes it from the older Língbǎo *zhāi*; the present fascicle is the *zhōngyuán* of that nine-fold structure.
